title: [Chapitre] III. Réseaux via découpages : notes manuscrites (08/06/1986).

deep.reconstruction:
Context: Chapter III, 'Réseaux via découpages' (1986). L is an ordered set, in practice a totally ordered set that is 'divisible' (dense) and directed upward and downward (no endpoints). Drop_k(L) appears to be the set of admissible k-element 'découpages' (cutting subsets) of L. The previous page proved a lemma deriving x ≤ u ≤ v ≤ y from betweenness data. Its NB says this used the distributivity of the order relation and the fact that L is directed upward and downward.

This page states the reconstruction programme. Suppose one is given L together with two relations:
- a binary relation R(a,b), meaning {a,b} ∈ Drop_2(L);
- a ternary relation R(a,b,c), meaning b is strictly between a and c.

Then, to reconstruct the order (up to reversal), it suffices to add that L is directed upward and downward. The struck lines tried to say more about filtrations and filters.

Grothendieck then announces a sharper claim. Knowing Drop_2(L), and for each ε ∈ Drop_2(L) knowing the set C(ε) = {t ∈ L − ε : ε ∪ {t} ∈ Drop_3(L)} with its decomposition into connected components, implies knowing the strict betweenness relation R(a,b,c).
- First necessary condition: {a,b,c} ∈ Drop_3(L). He notes in parentheses that this follows from the data Drop_2(L).
- Then, picturing a < b < c on a segment, he starts to look at a component J_abc of C({a,b}). That line is struck and restarted on p.15.

On p.15 the argument is completed. For each pair ε ⊂ J = {a,b,c}, let X_ε be the component of C(ε) containing the third point:
- X_{ab} = L_{>b}
- X_{bc} = L_{<b}
- X_{ca} = ]a,c[

The middle point b is the unique point of J for which the two X_ε with ε ∋ b are disjoint. The other intersections, ]b,c[ and ]a,b[, are nonempty by density ('divisibilité'). So betweenness, and hence the order up to duality, is recovered from the combinatorics of cuttings plus connectivity. This is part of an axiomatization of 1-dimensional 'lines' via their cuttings, presumably feeding into a theory of networks or arrangements ('réseaux').
errors: 'Connected components' of C(ε) must mean something intrinsic to the découpage data, or order-convex components. For a dense non-complete L such as Q, the order-topology components are singletons, so the argument would fail. If 'composante' presupposes the order, the reconstruction is circular. The page does not say which notion is meant.
The claim that {a,b,c} ∈ Drop_3(L) is determined by Drop_2(L) is asserted parenthetically without justification on this page.
The draft line defining J_abc is abandoned; the actual argument is on p.15 and relies on density (divisibility) for the nonemptiness of ]a,b[ and ]b,c[.

ideas.what: Recovering a total order (up to reversal) from the strict betweenness relation plus directedness
ideas.usually_credited_to: Pasch (1882), Huntington & Kline (1917), later Altwegg, Sholander

ideas.what: Characterizing the middle point of a triple via disjointness of components of complements of cut sets C(ε), using density
ideas.modern_name: reconstruction of linear order from cut/separation data (cf. separation relations, rank-2 chirotope-type axioms)
ideas.usually_credited_to: classical (separation and betweenness relations); oriented-matroid style axioms by Folkman–Lawrence / Bland–Las Vergnas

missed.claim: Part of an unpublished 1986 attempt to axiomatize 1-dimensional ordered 'lines' purely via the combinatorics of admissible cuttings (Drop_k) and connectivity, presumably as a foundation for 'réseaux' (networks or arrangements, perhaps of pseudo-lines). The page itself contains only an elementary reconstruction step.
missed.quote: la connaissance de ε ∈ Drop_2(L), de la donnée de C(ε) = { t ∈ L − ε | {ε,t} ∈ Drop_3(L)} [en] connexes, implique la connaissance de la relation R(a,b,c)
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: Of mainly historical interest. It documents Grothendieck's 1986 combinatorial-topological foundations, related in spirit to tame topology and pseudoline arrangements. The mathematical content is classical.

deep.surprise_reason: Elementary reconstruction of betweenness from cut data in a dense linear order. It is correct modulo the definition of components, and is classical in content; only its place in Grothendieck's 1986 'réseaux' project is noteworthy.
transcription_corrections: Line 1 likely reads 'Si on se donne : L puis les deux relations'.

'alors pour reconstituer le binaire[?]/la donnée, il suffit de savoir que L [est] filtrant croissant et filtrant décroissant'. Read 'filtrant' (directed) rather than 'filtration', consistent with the NB on p.13.
'On va voir que la connaissance de Drop_2(L), et pour ε ∈ Drop_2(L), de la donnée de C(ε)…' — 'de Drop_2(L)' appears to be partly struck or reworded.
